text:
maya: rolling up Mercator13B int4 onboarding notes — hitting reproducible OOMs at ~6k tokens with batch_size=4 and max_new_tokens=1024. kernel traces point to KV cache growth + fragmentation.
joel: seen similar pattern on other 13b quant models, usually around prefetched KV pages not being reclaimed.
sasha: can you paste the exact error?
maya: paste logs: ```[2025-07-12T14:03:21Z] OOM on device 0: alloc 1.2 GiB failed
  total used=47.1 GiB free=0.9 GiB
  context: forward_kv_cache_alloc -> prefetch_slot(4096)
  stack: runtime.cc:438 serve_request.cpp:92```
anil: interesting — free=0.9 GiB seems like fragmentation rather than full capacity. what's the allocator slab sizes?
maya: on 80GB A100, driver shows free chunks but non-contiguous. allocator=jemalloc with default arenas.
joel: two quick mitigations: 1) reduce default max_new_tokens from 1024 -> 512 for Mercator13B canary; 2) enforce micro-batching (split incoming batch 4 -> 2 with continuous batching)
sasha: also try turning on KV eviction heuristic for prefetched prefixes older than 128 tokens, that reclaimed 8GB in a previous run.
maya: ran a smoke with max_new_tokens=512 and batch_size=2 (client-side split). result: stable for 1k live requests, p95 latency +18% but no OOM.
infra-bot: deploy canary: mercator13b/int4 -> routing group merc-canary-1 status: success
anil: what's the quality delta from quant/int4 compared to fp16 baseline?
maya: ran eval on standard bench (LM-eval subset): rouge scores dropped ~0.9 points on long summarization prompts (>1024 context). Short prompts unchanged.
joel: that's within expected int4 noise. but we should also test whether batch-splitting + reduced max_new_tokens masks a regression (i.e., shorter responses may artificially improve scores).
sasha: propose a small test matrix:
- int4, max_new=512, batch=2
- int4, max_new=768, batch=2 with KV-evict=128
- int8, max_new=1024, batch=4
Run 200 eval samples each, compare latency, mem, and rouge.
maya: starting matrix run now. launching jobs on merc-canary-1.
joel: add a synthetic stress test: long priming prompt (system + 6 examples) + a 3k token continuation to try to recreate OOM.
anil: also capture fragmentation map: jemalloc stats + /proc/pid/smaps snapshot after warmup. we need to see whether compaction helps.
maya: uploaded jemalloc dump to S3: s3://rwinf-dev/mercator13b/jemalloc-dump-1748001234.txt
sasha: if compaction would help, we can try toggling arena_max_unmapped_bytes or enabling background purge. risky on prod but fine for canary.
joel: another low-risk operational tweak: add a per-route soft-slo that caps max_new_tokens for unknown clients (fallback to 256). reduces blast radius.
anil: note: padding and prefix caching are two contributors: long prefixes keep KV alive. consider aggressive prefix trimming for generative tasks where context beyond 2048 rarely helpful.
maya: results so far (quick summary):
- int4,512,batch2 -> stable, p95 latency 340ms, avg mem used 46.8 GiB, rouge -0.6
- int4,768,batch2,evict128 -> occasional OOM at scale (1/200 runs), p95 380ms, mem 47.6 GiB, rouge -0.7
- int8,1024,batch4 -> stable, p95 300ms, mem 52.9 GiB, rouge -0.2
sasha: that suggests int8 buys memory headroom as expected but higher cost. we should document a recommended preset: mercator13b-int4-lowmem: {max_new_tokens:512, batching:micro_batch=2, kv_evict_age:128, jemalloc_tweaks:background_purge=true}
joel: agree. also add a traffic routing fallback: if OOM rate > 0.5% in 10m window, promote to int8 automatically for new requests.
anil: for longer term: look at custom allocator or slot compactor in runtime to reduce fragmentation. filing infra ticket.
maya: filing followups:
- PR for default max_new_tokens change on mercator13b canary -> #PR-1392
- Ops runbook snippet for mercator13b low-mem preset (how to rollback to int8) -> GDrive link (shared)
- infra ticket for jemalloc compaction research -> INF-3421
sasha: I'll draft the canary playbook (inc. eval matrix, smoke steps, rollback) and ping security for the S3 artifacts.
joel: one last note — add a perf-counter to trace KV cache growth per request (tokens_in * kv_slots) so we can autotune eviction thresholds. small telemetry task.
maya: thanks all, will update thread with PR + canary link when ready. :thumbsup:
maya: (followup) PR merged, canary running at 5% traffic. will monitor mem and regression signals.
infra-bot: healthcheck merc-canary-1: p99 latency 1.2s, OOMs last 30m: 0, memory drift: +0.2 GiB/hour
joel: perfect. schedule 24h watch then widen to 20% if stable.
sasha: adding to onboarding checklist: "if quantized model shows >0.5pt rouge drop on long prompts, re-evaluate int8 or fine-tune with quant-aware calibration."
anil: tagging runtime folks for allocator deep-dive: @runtime-team
maya: end of thread — action items recorded.
